=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:66-71 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `git clone --branch "${resolver_ref}" --no-tags` cannot resolve raw SHA refs or tag refs, so the primary clone fails and the workflow falls back to `main`.
  WHY: All five reviewers reported this as a broken resolver staging path; severity is critical, and some noted the specific disagreement that this breaks both self-run SHA pinning and consumer `stable` tag resolution.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:66-71 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `2>/dev/null` suppresses all `git clone` stderr, hiding authentication, network, and ref-resolution failures.
  WHY: All reviewers agreed the workflow loses useful diagnostics and becomes hard to debug when staging fails.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:80-103 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The resolver step returns success and falls back when the staged resolver script is missing, masking a broken staging path.
  WHY: These reviewers said `exit 0` makes GitHub Actions report green even though the resolver did not stage correctly; severity is the highest reported across reviewers.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:66-104 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The staged resolver directory is created under `RUNNER_TEMP` but never cleaned up after use.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed this can accumulate disk usage on self-hosted runners, though they differed on priority and impact.
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:71-77 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The disallowed marker `base64 --decode >` is overly broad and can false-positive on unrelated legitimate base64 usage.
  WHY: Both reviewers identified the same test fragility rooted in the same substring match; severity is kept at the highest reported by these reviewers.
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:69-87 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The audit test is too brittle because it relies on exact string matching for the canonical stage line and rejects harmless formatting differences.
  WHY: Both reviewers pointed to the same root cause: valid YAML/shell quoting or spacing changes could fail the test even when semantics are unchanged.
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:89-90 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The test only checks for string presence and does not verify the `git clone` logic is actually correct.
  WHY: This is a singleton finding; it was not duplicated elsewhere, so it remains separate in consensus.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and implement.yml, orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml, plan.yml, validate.yml):66-71 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `git clone --branch "${resolver_ref}"` cannot checkout SHA refs, and `--no-tags` prevents tag resolution.
  WHY: When `resolver_ref` is a SHA (self-repo mode) or `stable` tag (consumer mode), the clone fails and the workflow falls back to `main` instead of using the intended resolver version.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other workflow files):66-71 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `2>/dev/null` suppresses stderr output from `git clone`, hiding authentication/network/ref resolution errors.
  WHY: Debugging clone failures becomes difficult as error messages are hidden.
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:73 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `"base64 --decode >"` in `disallowed_inline_markers` is overly broad and could match legitimate base64 decoding unrelated to resolver staging.
  WHY: The test could fail on valid code that uses base64 decoding for other purposes.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and `plan.yml`, `implement.yml`, `orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml`, `validate.yml`):66-71 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new logic uses `git clone --branch <ref> --no-tags`, which is incompatible with both `${{ github.sha }}` and the `stable` tag.
  WHY: Git cannot clone a raw SHA as a branch, and `--no-tags` prevents tag resolution, so the workflow always falls back to `main`.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and others):95-103 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The temporary directory `${resolver_stage_root}` is never deleted after `bash "${resolver_script}"` runs.
  WHY: Each run creates a new directory under `${RUNNER_TEMP}` that persists indefinitely, which can leak disk space on self-hosted runners.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and others):85-88 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The step exits successfully even when the resolver script is missing, masking staging failures.
  WHY: The workflow reports success and silently falls back to the default branch, which hides broken resolver deployment.
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:69, 73 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The audit test is too rigid on formatting and too broad on disallowed markers.
  WHY: Exact-string checks can fail on harmless YAML/shell formatting changes, and `base64 --decode >` can false-positive on legitimate use.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and duplicated in implement.yml, orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml, plan.yml, validate.yml):66-71 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `git clone --branch` cannot resolve a commit SHA or a tag when `--no-tags` is used, so the primary clone always fails.
  WHY: Self-run mode uses `${{ github.sha }}` and consumer mode uses `stable`, but both cases force a fallback to `main`, making the staged resolver unusable.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and duplicated in implement.yml, orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml, plan.yml, validate.yml): All clone commands use `2>/dev/null` | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The stderr from `git clone` is discarded, hiding authentication, network, and ref-resolution errors.
  WHY: Without diagnostics, operators cannot determine why staging failed and only see a generic warning.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and duplicated in implement.yml, orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml, plan.yml, validate.yml):80-83 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The step exits with code 0 when the resolver script is missing.
  WHY: GitHub Actions reports success even though resolver staging failed, so broken deployment is masked.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and duplicated in implement.yml, orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml, plan.yml, validate.yml): resolver_stage_root cleanup | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The staging directory is cleaned at the start but never removed after the resolver runs.
  WHY: On shared or self-hosted runners, cloned repositories accumulate in `${RUNNER_TEMP}` and can exhaust disk space.
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:73 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `base64 --decode >` pattern is too broad and can flag unrelated legitimate base64 usage.
  WHY: This can create false positives in otherwise valid workflow content.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

  WHY: Authentication, network, and ref-resolution failures become opaque, severely degrading observability.

  WHY: This can produce spurious CI failures on benign workflow content.
